By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Further information:
Crashes not Accidents.

Initial story
Low Conviction Rate of DUI accidents.

New development?

https://www.iol.co.za/motoring/industry-news/7-day-jail-plan-for-drunk-drivers-is-absurd-jpsa-17805203
https://businesstech.co.za/news/lifestyle/282159/plan-for-tougher-punishment-for-drunk-drivers-is-a-joke-legal-expert/
If we go this route an interview with Dr James Grant - Wits Law.

Also, 7 day jail plan for drunk driving

All traffic offences schedules up to Schedule 5, like tail light broken.

Sympathy of school of thought ,drunk drivers burden on society.

Muderer 48 hours before brought before court.

AARTO act guilty until proven innocent.

Crash not accident terminology

Is it an “accident” when you get behind the wheel of a car, knowing that you have been drinking?
Last year 86 160 cases of driving under influence were reported, a figure that increased by 14.8% from the previous year. Clearly there are not enough incentives to curb drink driving. And with a conviction rate between 7-11% there is the likely chance that you will get away with it in SA.

Case Studies.

Archy Archary (Accident happened in Durban, they live in Midrand)
6 Greyston
17 Princeton Rd
Vorna valley
Wednesday 21st of Nov

On the 17th of June 2017 at 10:30 we were hit from behind by a drunk driver while stationary at a red traffic light in Durban visiting their parents. Taariqa Archary (30 - Electronic Engineer) and Varsha Maharaj (26 - Attorney) were sitting in the back seat and both suffered serious life changing injuries. Taariqa is now a quadriplegic and Varsha has brain damage with severe memory loss, excruciating headaches and fatigue. Archy says,”We have followed the criminal case closely and found that the state prosecutors have been undermining our rights to close the case quickly and get their completion rates up. First, I was told that the case has nothing to do with us and that I must sit in the back of the court and shut up. I learnt that a plea bargain was being concluded without the victims consent. I went to the senior public prosecutor to explain the seriousness of our injuries and stop the plea bargain.”

The accused fled the scene of the crime. An off duty policeman saw him leaving the scene and followed him for 30 km. Blood tests were taken - 0.26 (five times over limit).
Cnr Soldier’s Way and Ordanance. 10:30





The accused has been given a 3 year sentence for fleeing the scene and only 6 months or R 10 000 for DUI. He is appealing this sentence.

(Blood at St Augustines Stefan Bothma)
Constable Wynand Last 0713507446
Captain Elizabeth Squires 0835550394
Brigadier Naiker 0825567865
deBeerS@saps.gov.za (Sent email requesting interview)
I have tasked Colonel Brenda Muridili to attend to your request. Her e-mail address is MuridiliB@saps.gov.za and her contact number is 071 686 94225

State prosecutor did not request an interview with them. They approached Senior State Prosecutor, after the State Prosecutor told them that all they had to do was keep quiet and sit in the back of the court. They have not looked at a civil claim.


Second Case Study Franschoek

Martin Webb’s son, Anthony, was killed on Bastille Day in July 2016. Anthony was partially to blame, as he borrowed an off road bike and had been drinking himself. He was driving past La Motte wine farm when Hendrik Anthony Stolk hit him with his car. Stolk had been drinking at Tukkies bar in Stellenbosch. We have video footage of this. The manager will say how much he had been drinking. Although Stolk was encouraged not to drive by the manager of the bar, he ignored him and left in his car. Apparently in the footage you can see Stolk over taking cars on a solid white line and then hitting Anthony Webb, when he veered back into the left hand lane again.

He said that he did not see Anthony. (It is well known that one’s vision is impaired by drink.) The police did not take any blood tests from Stolk. (Ironically the victim had blood tests done at his post mortem.) The day after this incident, the perpetrator was seen again drinking at the bar again.

Because of lack of interest by the police, Anthony’s dad paid a private accident expert to recreate the accident so that his expertise could be presented to the court.

In court Stolk was found guilty of culpable homicide and given a year suspended sentence and a R 12 000 fine. When Martin was in court, the case that was heard before him was of a thief that had stolen a box of chocolates. He was given a R 2000 fine. Martin said it felt as though his son’s life was only worth 6 boxes of chocolates.

Research Notes

"Different Jail time sentencing not comprehensible"

South Africans Against Drunk Driving feels the Justice system shows leniency to road traffic crimes. Although we acknowledge that jail sentences have recently been given we question if they are harsh enough to deter future negligent drivers. A Pietermaritzburg cancer con artist and fraudster got a 10 years jail sentence whereas a Durban hit and run drunk driver who caused brain injuries to a candidate attorney and left an electronic engineer quadriplegic, was only given a 3-year jail sentence and a R10 000 fine. Magistrate Bhengu implied this was a harsh sentence for the severe injuries and said “Statistics showed that South Africa had the highest drunk driving incident rates in the world. Our roads are the most dangerous in the world. It is my view that drunk driving cases are not being taken seriously." SADD do not agree that his sentence was harsh. Legally the Magistrate could have given the allowed 12-year jail sentence per injury and a R120 000 fine. Recently a Durban drinking, reckless and negligent driver got 5 years jail sentence per cyclist he killed (2 dead = 10 years jail time ). Magistrate Singh said ”The number of people who lose their lives in road accidents in this country is unacceptably high… it's beyond comprehension. I believe this case is an opportunity to impose an exemplary sentence… to warn potential offenders that this is what could happen to them if they behave negligently."

DUI Script

V/O
Many South Africans feel that there is little harm in having a few drinks at a social event and getting into your car to drive home.

Link GIVE THIS STAT A TITLE
Every year in SA about 18 000 are killed and a 150 000 are injured in road accidents. Alcohol causes 60% of these crashes twice the world average.

V/O
Drivers are getting away with reckless behaviour. With a conviction rate of around 11% it’s time to reign it in, says and it the Road Traffic Management Corporation’s CEO, Adv Makhosini Msibi.

Msibi
“People believe that its normal if I drink and drive, it’s normal nothing will happen.

V/O
On the eve of the festive season, Adv Misibi is initiating a controversial proposal to the Justice department to re classify drunk driving, reckless and negligent driving from a Schedule 2 to a Schedule 5 offence in the same category as murder, rape and robbery.

Msibi
“Well we know we have attracted a lot of backlash, a lot of dissatisfaction in order to change the behaviour.”

V/O
He is also proposing that instead of the police granting you bail you will be imprisoned for 7 days and make a bail application to the court.

Msibi
“Yes we acknowledge that you need to have your freedom but we also go a step further to say can we keep you. Have a bail, a formal bail to say can we keep you within 7 days or before 7 days.

V/O
Hamresin Archary has had his family’s life irrevocably changed by a drunk driver. He’s in favour of Adv Msibi’s proposal.

Claire
“We always hear these stories of people drinking and driving do you think there’s enough of a deterrant to stop this bad behaviour.”

Hamresin
“Absolutely not , we have to have strong examples of where the law works and where people are not only terrified of the consequences on their part but are terrified of what they can do to people’s lives.”

V/O
Hamresin and his wife Taariqa’s life was changed beyond recognition in June 2017. Constable Wynand Laatz was off duty and on his way home.

Laatz
“On my way home I noticed a car flying past us, all over the place, really notice something not right. Within a minute of saying that this vehicle crashed into the back of another car.”

Up sound screech.

Archy
“While stationery out of nowehere we were hit from behind from a speeding vehicle, without brakes there was no tire squeal, instant impact.

V/O
Hamresin was in the car with his wife Taariqa and her two sisters.

Archy
“I immediately screamed is everyone OK, my wife was squashed up behind the front seat and her arms in a spasm and they were shaking and she was unconscious for a while. My sister in law was unconscious for a frighteningly long time.”


V/O
26 year old Fitness Instructor Stephan Bothma rammed into the back of the Archary’s car. Bothma was found to be 5 times over the blood alcohol limit. Without checking to see if he’d caused any injuries, he fled the scene of the accident.

Constable Laatz gave chase.

Laatz
“We probably did speed in excess of 130 km per hour, eventually after 33 kms chasing after at 11 oclock at night
stop on Kassia road bridge . Immediatey noticed that he was under the influence way stumbling and smell of alcohol and placed him under arrest.”

V/O
Hamresin was uninjured but the two back passengers were rushed to hospital. His sister in law suffered a brain injury. His wife’s vertebra was fractured. She had spinal cord compression which has left her a quadraplegic and wheelchair bound.

Taariqa
“My best friend came to see me and I said I can’t move. Why can’t I move? “

V/O
For the Archary’s it was pure luck that the perpetrator was caught.

Laatz
“If I wasn’t there he would have gotten away with it, no one would have been able to get his blood level , alcohol level totally different ball game.”

V/O
3 months later Hamresin went to court to seek justice.

Hamresin
“I approached the state proesecutor in the morning and said we want to assist wherever we can. There were very serious injuries as a result of this accident.And the next thing she said to me was Oh but nothing you are going do here is going to change that. You can sit in the back of the court room and shut up.”
Claire
“What?”
Hamresin
“That was first interaction with State prosecutor who was fighting this case. “

V/O
He complained to the senior public prosecutor and the case was reassigned. Bothma pleaded guilty to drunk driving and failing to perform the duties of a driver by fleeing the scene. He was given a 3 year sentence and fined R10 000 or 10 months, half of which was suspended. He is appealing this sentence.

Link REDO IN V/O
We have 11 million vehicles on our road and only 23 000 thousand TRAFFIC OFFICERS to monitor them all. This huge imbalance favours the offenders whose chances of being caught are slim.

V/O
The Western Cape has introduced Evidentiary Breath Alcohol Testing or EBAT, which shows promise as it speeds up the system and improves the conviction rate. EBAT gives immediate results that can be used as evidence in court. No further blood tests are needed. Blood test results can often be delayed up to a year.

V/O
The Athlone Shadow Testing station is open 24 hours a day

Link
Together with the mobile units these testings stations have been able to increase the drunk driving conviction rate in the Western Cape.

V/O
Donald Grant is the MEC for Transport and Public Works and says EBAT is changing drivers behaviour’.

Donald
“We have seen a shift from over 3% of drivers being over the limit to now we are at a .8 percent , which is a fantastic improvement. More than 200%, australia screen is at 0.2 and although we are not at world standard by a long way there is certainly a huge improvement
in behaviour change.

V/O
There are many links in the chain of evidence that have to be beyond reproach to get more convictions, says Dr James Grant, a practising advocate.

James Grant
Father of criminology wrote it is not the severity of punishment that reduces crime it is the certainty of punishment. If it was case of that you knew without question that the chances of you being stopped in a road block are extremely high, who would drive drunk. People would immediately change their behaviours.

V/O
Adv Msibi believe that not only new tighter legislation but a nationwide EBAT system will change behaviour. Four stationery and four mobile units have been launched in Gauteng.

Msibi
“The Ebat system gives us immediate results of the content within your blood so we deal with it expediciously.
because these people go to jail because that is where they belong. If you consume liquor you must appreciate the consequences.”


V/O
Msibi has also committed to upskilling officers with a 3 year course.
Had the policeman been properly trained, he would have known to take blood when Martyn Webb’s son, Anthony was killed in a motor accident 2 years ago after the Bastille Day celebration in Franschoek.

Claire
“You get the phone call that every parent dreads”

Martyn
“My daughter Vivienne had just informed us that Anthony had just been killed. It’s just an empty horrible feeling, you just cry and cry and cry.”

V/O
On security camera footage at a popular bar in Franschoek, 56 year old Michael Stolk is seen buying drinks throughout the day.

V/O Accident
Anthony was also was heading home, he’d been drinking and he was on the road illegally on an off road bike and his lights were not on.
A camera outside a wine farm captured the detail.

At about 6:20 at twilight Michael Stolk crossed a solid white line at 128 km/h to overtake the slower cars…he crashes into Anthony Webb who was traveling in the opposite direction.

Martyn
“If you get in a car and you are under the influence . It’s no better than a person who takes a gun and shoots you. It’s exactly the same thing. It’s criminal.”

V/O
A sentiment that Caro Smit echoes. She started an NGO called South Africans against Drunk Driving when her son, Chas, was killed by a drunken driver.

Caro
“The terminology needs to change from accidents to crashes. It’s not an accident of someone has been drinking and they drive or driving or if they are speeding or negligent.”

V/O
Anthony was killed instantly. And according to their lawyer Eric Louw the criminal justice system let them down.

Eric
“Now it starts with the policenot making arrest not taking the blood, not have the proper training, shortage of staff. Then it goes on to medical practitioner not drawing the blood properly, not keeping the sample properly. Then it moves on to prosecution servicesand our totally overburdened and our court rolls are totally clogged. So there’s various issues experienced in the criminal justice system.


V/O
The magistrate convicted him of culpable homicide and gave him a R 12 000 fine and a 5 year suspended sentence.

Caro
We need to really stop this incredible road carnarge nd talk about the victims who are left behind the severly injured and also the victims, my life has beenchanged forever.

Martyn
‘Somebody died, the police failed to take that man’s blood we can’t carry on like this in South Africa anymore.

Taariqa
“I question myself just sitting here not able to do anything. It’s just literally what I do is breathing. Do you call that living?”


Promo 1 x 10 secs
The Road Traffic Management Corporation is proposing that anyone caught drinking and driving should spend at least 7 days in jail before they can be considered for bail. A sobering thought (this festive season).

Promo 2 x 15 seconds

South Africa has one of the highest incidents of drunk driving in the world. The Road Traffic Management Agency is proposing changing legislation, to classify DUI in the same category as murder, rape and robbery.

Promo 3 x 15 Seconds

Martyn Webb’s son Anthony was killed on the road by a drunk driver. Are you willing to have one for the road this festive season?

Martyn
“If you get in a car and you are under the influence . It’s no better than a person who takes a gun and shoots you. It’s exactly the same thing. It’s criminal.”



Promo 4 x 30 seconds


UPSOUND a VICTIM:

V/O Thousands of people die on the road because of drunk drivers.

Msibi “People believe that its normal if I drink and drive, it’s normal nothing will happen.

Now the Road Traffic Management Corporation wants to change that. Adv Makhosini Msibi is campaigning for the justice department to make drunk driving from a schedule 2 to a schedule 5 offence and keep the drivers for 7 days before bail.

Msibi “If you consume liquor you must appreciate the consequences.”

Our roads are the most dangerous in the world. It is my view that drunk driving cases are not being taken seriously." SADD do not agree that his sentence was harsh. Legally the Magistrate could have given the allowed 12-year jail sentence per injury and a R120 000 fine. Recently a Durban drinking, reckless and negligent driver got 5 years jail sentence per cyclist he killed (2 dead = 10 years jail time ). Magistrate Singh said ”The number of people who lose their lives in road accidents in this country is unacceptably high… it's beyond comprehension. I believe this case is an opportunity to impose an exemplary sentence… to warn potential offenders that this is what could happen to them if they behave negligently." December 2018 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 07 December 2018 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: DUI Script V/O Many South Africans feel that there is little harm in having a few drinks at a social event and getting into your car to drive home. Link GIVE THIS STAT A TITLE Every year in SA about 18 000 are killed and a 150 000 are injured in road accidents. Alcohol causes 60% of these crashes twice the world average. V/O Drivers are getting away with reckless behaviour. With a conviction rate of around 11% it’s time to reign it in, says and it the Road Traffic Management Corporation’s CEO, Adv Makhosini Msibi. Msibi “People believe that its normal if I drink and drive, it’s normal nothing will happen. V/O On the eve of the festive season, Adv Misibi is initiating a controversial proposal to the Justice department to re classify drunk driving, reckless and negligent driving from a Schedule 2 to a Schedule 5 offence in the same category as murder, rape and robbery. Msibi “Well we know we have attracted a lot of backlash, a lot of dissatisfaction in order to change the behaviour.” V/O He is also proposing that instead of the police granting you bail you will be imprisoned for 7 days and make a bail application to the court. Msibi “Yes we acknowledge that you need to have your freedom but we also go a step further to say can we keep you. Have a bail, a formal bail to say can we keep you within 7 days or before 7 days. V/O Hamresin Archary has had his family’s life irrevocably changed by a drunk driver. He’s in favour of Adv Msibi’s proposal. Claire “We always hear these stories of people drinking and driving do you think there’s enough of a deterrant to stop this bad behaviour.” Hamresin “Absolutely not , we have to have strong examples of where the law works and where people are not only terrified of the consequences on their part but are terrified of what they can do to people’s lives.” V/O Hamresin and his wife Taariqa’s life was changed beyond recognition in June 2017. Constable Wynand Laatz was off duty and on his way home. Laatz “On my way home I noticed a car flying past us, all over the place, really notice something not right. Within a minute of saying that this vehicle crashed into the back of another car.” Up sound screech. Archy “While stationery out of nowehere we were hit from behind from a speeding vehicle, without brakes there was no tire squeal, instant impact. V/O Hamresin was in the car with his wife Taariqa and her two sisters. Archy “I immediately screamed is everyone OK, my wife was squashed up behind the front seat and her arms in a spasm and they were shaking and she was unconscious for a while. My sister in law was unconscious for a frighteningly long time.” V/O 26 year old Fitness Instructor Stephan Bothma rammed into the back of the Archary’s car. Bothma was found to be 5 times over the blood alcohol limit. Without checking to see if he’d caused any injuries, he fled the scene of the accident. Constable Laatz gave chase. Laatz “We probably did speed in excess of 130 km per hour, eventually after 33 kms chasing after at 11 oclock at night stop on Kassia road bridge . Immediatey noticed that he was under the influence way stumbling and smell of alcohol and placed him under arrest.” V/O Hamresin was uninjured but the two back passengers were rushed to hospital. His sister in law suffered a brain injury. His wife’s vertebra was fractured. She had spinal cord compression which has left her a quadraplegic and wheelchair bound. Taariqa “My best friend came to see me and I said I can’t move. Why can’t I move? “ V/O For the Archary’s it was pure luck that the perpetrator was caught. Laatz “If I wasn’t there he would have gotten away with it, no one would have been able to get his blood level , alcohol level totally different ball game.” V/O 3 months later Hamresin went to court to seek justice. Hamresin “I approached the state proesecutor in the morning and said we want to assist wherever we can. There were very serious injuries as a result of this accident.And the next thing she said to me was Oh but nothing you are going do here is going to change that. You can sit in the back of the court room and shut up.” Claire “What?” Hamresin “That was first interaction with State prosecutor who was fighting this case. “ V/O He complained to the senior public prosecutor and the case was reassigned. Bothma pleaded guilty to drunk driving and failing to perform the duties of a driver by fleeing the scene. He was given a 3 year sentence and fined R10 000 or 10 months, half of which was suspended. He is appealing this sentence. Link REDO IN V/O We have 11 million vehicles on our road and only 23 000 thousand TRAFFIC OFFICERS to monitor them all. This huge imbalance favours the offenders whose chances of being caught are slim. V/O The Western Cape has introduced Evidentiary Breath Alcohol Testing or EBAT, which shows promise as it speeds up the system and improves the conviction rate. EBAT gives immediate results that can be used as evidence in court. No further blood tests are needed. Blood test results can often be delayed up to a year. V/O The Athlone Shadow Testing station is open 24 hours a day Link Together with the mobile units these testings stations have been able to increase the drunk driving conviction rate in the Western Cape. V/O Donald Grant is the MEC for Transport and Public Works and says EBAT is changing drivers behaviour’. Donald “We have seen a shift from over 3% of drivers being over the limit to now we are at a .8 percent , which is a fantastic improvement. More than 200%, australia screen is at 0.2 and although we are not at world standard by a long way there is certainly a huge improvement in behaviour change. V/O There are many links in the chain of evidence that have to be beyond reproach to get more convictions, says Dr James Grant, a practising advocate. James Grant Father of criminology wrote it is not the severity of punishment that reduces crime it is the certainty of punishment. If it was case of that you knew without question that the chances of you being stopped in a road block are extremely high, who would drive drunk. People would immediately change their behaviours. V/O Adv Msibi believe that not only new tighter legislation but a nationwide EBAT system will change behaviour. Four stationery and four mobile units have been launched in Gauteng. Msibi “The Ebat system gives us immediate results of the content within your blood so we deal with it expediciously. because these people go to jail because that is where they belong. If you consume liquor you must appreciate the consequences.” V/O Msibi has also committed to upskilling officers with a 3 year course. Had the policeman been properly trained, he would have known to take blood when Martyn Webb’s son, Anthony was killed in a motor accident 2 years ago after the Bastille Day celebration in Franschoek. Claire “You get the phone call that every parent dreads” Martyn “My daughter Vivienne had just informed us that Anthony had just been killed. It’s just an empty horrible feeling, you just cry and cry and cry.” V/O On security camera footage at a popular bar in Franschoek, 56 year old Michael Stolk is seen buying drinks throughout the day. V/O Accident Anthony was also was heading home, he’d been drinking and he was on the road illegally on an off road bike and his lights were not on. A camera outside a wine farm captured the detail. At about 6:20 at twilight Michael Stolk crossed a solid white line at 128 km/h to overtake the slower cars…he crashes into Anthony Webb who was traveling in the opposite direction. Martyn “If you get in a car and you are under the influence . It’s no better than a person who takes a gun and shoots you. It’s exactly the same thing. It’s criminal.” V/O A sentiment that Caro Smit echoes. She started an NGO called South Africans against Drunk Driving when her son, Chas, was killed by a drunken driver. Caro “The terminology needs to change from accidents to crashes. It’s not an accident of someone has been drinking and they drive or driving or if they are speeding or negligent.” V/O Anthony was killed instantly. And according to their lawyer Eric Louw the criminal justice system let them down. Eric “Now it starts with the policenot making arrest not taking the blood, not have the proper training, shortage of staff. Then it goes on to medical practitioner not drawing the blood properly, not keeping the sample properly. Then it moves on to prosecution servicesand our totally overburdened and our court rolls are totally clogged. So there’s various issues experienced in the criminal justice system. V/O The magistrate convicted him of culpable homicide and gave him a R 12 000 fine and a 5 year suspended sentence. Caro We need to really stop this incredible road carnarge nd talk about the victims who are left behind the severly injured and also the victims, my life has beenchanged forever. Martyn ‘Somebody died, the police failed to take that man’s blood we can’t carry on like this in South Africa anymore. Taariqa “I question myself just sitting here not able to do anything. It’s just literally what I do is breathing. Do you call that living?” Promo 1 x 10 secs The Road Traffic Management Corporation is proposing that anyone caught drinking and driving should spend at least 7 days in jail before they can be considered for bail. A sobering thought (this festive season). Promo 2 x 15 seconds South Africa has one of the highest incidents of drunk driving in the world. The Road Traffic Management Agency is proposing changing legislation, to classify DUI in the same category as murder, rape and robbery. Promo 3 x 15 Seconds Martyn Webb’s son Anthony was killed on the road by a drunk driver. Are you willing to have one for the road this festive season? Martyn “If you get in a car and you are under the influence . It’s no better than a person who takes a gun and shoots you. It’s exactly the same thing. It’s criminal.” Promo 4 x 30 seconds UPSOUND a VICTIM: V/O Thousands of people die on the road because of drunk drivers. Msibi “People believe that its normal if I drink and drive, it’s normal nothing will happen. Now the Road Traffic Management Corporation wants to change that. Adv Makhosini Msibi is campaigning for the justice department to make drunk driving from a schedule 2 to a schedule 5 offence and keep the drivers for 7 days before bail.
